mechanism_narrative: A persistent increase in the Federal Funds rate above 2.5% over the prior 3 months reduces the present value of future equity cash flows, thereby depressing S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: FEDFUNDS crosses above 2.5% in a 3-month window
failure_condition: 20-day forward returns are positive despite FEDFUNDS > 2.5% for 3 months, or IC > 0.05 over the horizon.

mechanism_narrative: Rising employment momentum as measured by PAYEMS (monthly payroll gains) coincides with stronger consumer confidence and higher wage growth, driving S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 days.
candidate_trigger: PAYEMS increases by at least 2% month-over-month for two consecutive months
failure_condition: SPX 60-day forward returns are negative despite PAYEMS growth > 2% MoM for 2 months.

mechanism_narrative: A sharp contraction in industrial production (GDPC1) followed by a rebound above the prior quarter's level indicates a turning point in supply-side constraints, prompting S&P 500 forward returns to turn positive over the next 20 days.
candidate_trigger: GDPC1 shows a double-bottom pattern (QoQ decline then rebound)
failure_condition: No statistically significant return to positive 20-day forward returns after the rebound.

mechanism_narrative: When the Industrial Production index (INDPRO) exceeds 104.0 for two consecutive months, it reflects supply-chain normalization, which reduces term premium and supports S&P 500 forward returns over the next 5 days.
candidate_trigger: INDPRO crosses and holds above 104.0 for 2 months
failure_condition: 5-day forward returns are negative despite INDPRO > 104.0 for 2 months.

mechanism_narrative: Consecutive months of declining Consumer Price Index (CPIAUCSL) below 236.0 suggest deflationary pressure, lowering real discount rates and generating negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 days.
candidate_trigger: CPIAUCSL declines for three consecutive months below 236.0
failure_condition: 20-day forward returns are positive despite CPIAUCSL < 236.0 for 3 months.

mechanism_narrative: A sudden spike in unemployment benefits claims (PAYEMS) followed by a sustained drop indicates labor market softening, which typically precedes a bearish S&P 500 20-day forward move.
candidate_trigger: PAYEMS increases by >10% in a single month then declines for two months
failure_condition: 20-day forward returns remain flat or positive despite the softening labor signal.

mechanism_narrative: Concurrent declines in both the unemployment rate (UNRATE) and the 10-year Treasury yield (implied by FEDFUNDS) create a dual tailwind for equity valuations, producing positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 days when both conditions hold.
candidate_trigger: UNRATE < 5.0% AND FEDFUNDS < 1.5% for the prior 30 days
regime_hint: low inflation and low rate environment
failure_condition: 60-day forward returns are negative despite UNRATE < 5.0% and FEDFUNDS < 1.5% for 30 days.

mechanism_narrative: During a post-crisis normalization regime (defined by HOUST > 1100 and UNRATE < 6.0%), S&P 500 forward returns tend to be positive over the next 20 days as market participants anticipate sustained economic expansion.
failure_condition: 20-day forward returns are negative in the regime while the regime conditions persist.
